items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Ralph Sutton told me that Fats Waller said

ctx.x: Didn’t Fats Waller or somebody say if you have to ask that question you’ll never know or something like that.
Ralph Sutton told me that Fats Waller said, “get that right ticking rhythm and it’s happening” or something like that. I actually like the fact that certain things can’t be defined.

Yeah, well it’s got to be felt. How do you define love? I don’t ever tell — a lot of guys, I mean the more you say “I love you” the less it means. I mean ending every phone call to a grandchild or to your son — some people say it ad nauseum. You can’t end your conversation with “I love you.” It’s like Edwin R. Murrow saying “good night and good luck.” And I never say “I love you” to my sons. They don’t need to know that. I don’t need to remind them. I don’t say it to my grandchildren. But I got a Father’s Day card
